content.summary: This chapter provides an overview of the FastAPI RAG architecture, explaining its purpose, users, and how its main components fit together.

blocks.text: Overview of FastAPI RAG Architecture
DocQA is a retrieval-augmented question answering system over uploaded documents backed by PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and Redis [E2][E15][E16][E17].
Main API Endpoints and Flows
The application provides endpoints for document management. For instance, uploading a document triggers an ingestion service and enqueues a background job [E3].

items: upload_document receives the file and database/queue dependencies [E3].
get_db yields a database session per request [E1].
get_queue returns an arq Redis pool used to enqueue background jobs [E2].
get_settings retrieves the cached runtime configuration [E5].
Settings defines the configuration options for the API and worker [E4].
IngestionService owns the document lifecycle in PostgreSQL and Qdrant [E6].

blocks.text: The application relies on FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Qdrant client, OpenAI, sentence-transformers, rank-bm25, arq, Redis, and pypdf [E16].
Configuration and Services
Runtime configuration for the API and the worker is loaded via Pydantic BaseSettings, which configures database_url, redis_url, qdrant_url, and embedding options [E4].

blocks.code:
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """Runtime configuration for the API and the worker."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    database_url: str = "postgresql+asyncpg://docqa:<REDACTED_SECRET>@localhost:5432/docqa"
    redis_url: str = "redis://localhost:6379/0"
    qdrant_url: str = "http://localhost:6333"
    collection_name: str = "docqa_chunks"
    openai_api_key: str = DEV_OPENAI_API_KEY
    chat_model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
    embedding_model: str = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
    embedding_dim: int = 384
    chunk_size: int = 800
    chunk_overlap: int = 120
    top_k: int = 8
    log_level: str = "INFO"
    cors_origins: list[str] = ["http://localhost:3000"]
blocks.caption: Settings

blocks.text: API Request Lifecycle and Routing

Building on the concepts introduced in Overview of FastAPI RAG Architecture, this chapter explores how requests are routed and handled within the fastapi_rag application. Other topics such as data models and persistence, background processing and tasks, configuration and deployment setup, and database migrations and versions are covered in other chapters.
Exposed Routes and Handlers
The service exposes multiple endpoints for health checks, document management, and querying. For instance, the health check endpoint reports that the API process is alive [E1].

blocks.caption: Health check route

blocks.text: Request Flows
When a request hits an endpoint, it passes through FastAPI dependencies and service layers before returning a response.

items: The client sends a request to DELETE /documents/{document_id} [E3].
The delete_document route handler is invoked [E3].
The get_db dependency yields a database session [E2].
SessionLocal creates the asynchronous session instance [E2].
IngestionService is instantiated with the database session [E3].
IngestionService.delete_document is called to remove the document [E3].
IngestionService.get_document fetches the target document [E6].
VectorStore.delete_document removes associated vectors from Qdrant [E12].
The database session commits the deletion [E6].

content.summary: This chapter details the data models and persistence stores used in fastapi_rag.

blocks.text: Data Models and Persistence
Building upon Overview of FastAPI RAG Architecture, this chapter explores where fastapi_rag stores its data and how the code interacts with those stores.
Data Stores and Models
The project uses SQLAlchemy models for documents and chunks stored in PostgreSQL [E2]. The base class for models is defined using DeclarativeBase [E3].
The Chunk model is a retrievable slice of a document defined with SQLAlchemy, having an id, document_id, position, text, and token_count [E12].
Reading and Writing Stores
Services such as IngestionService and HybridRetriever interact with the database sessions and vector stores.

content.summary: Background processing in fastapi_rag is handled by arq workers that consume tasks to chunk, embed, and index uploaded documents.

blocks.text: Background Processing and Tasks

Building upon Overview of FastAPI RAG Architecture, this chapter explores how background jobs, workers, and queues manage asynchronous processing in the fastapi_rag repository. Topics such as API request routing, database persistence, configuration, and migrations are covered in other chapters.
Worker Configuration and Startup
The project uses arq for background job queuing and processing. The worker configuration is defined in app/workers/tasks.py through the WorkerSettings class [E2].

blocks.code:
class WorkerSettings:
    """arq worker configuration."""

    functions = [ingest_document]
    on_startup = startup
    redis_settings = RedisSettings.from_dsn(get_settings().redis_url)
    max_jobs = 4
blocks.caption: WorkerSettings definition

blocks.text: When the worker starts up, it logs a startup message via the startup function [E1].

blocks.code:
async def startup(ctx: dict) -> None:
    logger.info("worker starting")
blocks.caption: Worker startup function

blocks.text: Ingestion Task Execution Flow
The primary background task is ingest_document, which handles chunking, embedding, and indexing for uploaded documents [E3]. Here is the step-by-step execution flow for processing a document:

items: The queue consumer invokes ingest_document with context and a document_id [E3].
A new database session is created using SessionLocal [E3].
An IngestionService instance is initialized with the session [E3].
IngestionService.ingest is called with the document_id [E3].
IngestionService.get_document fetches the document and its chunks from the database [E7].
The raw text is split into pieces using split_text [E8].

blocks.text: The project uses arq for background tasks, with worker settings configured in WorkerSettings specifying functions such as ingest_document, startup hooks, Redis settings, and a maximum of 4 jobs [E2]. Background jobs are enqueued using an arq Redis pool created via get_queue [E10].

blocks.text: Application Initialization and Flow
When the API service starts, the application builds via create_app, which retrieves configuration settings and configures middleware and routers [E3].

blocks.code:
def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    """Build the FastAPI application."""
    settings = get_settings()
    application = FastAPI(title="DocQA", version="0.3.1", lifespan=lifespan)
    application.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    application.include_router(api_router, prefix="/api/v1")
    return application
blocks.caption: create_app function

blocks.text: The initialization follows a strict execution path starting from app/main.py:

items: app/main.py starts the initialization [E3].
create_app builds the FastAPI application instance [E3].
get_settings fetches runtime configurations [E2].
Settings returns the loaded parameters [E1].

blocks.text: Additionally, a lifespan asynchronous context manager handles startup and shutdown tasks such as setting up the Qdrant collection and disposing of the database engine [E7].

blocks.code:
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Create the Qdrant collection on startup and dispose the DB engine on shutdown."""
    settings = get_settings()
    configure_logging(settings.log_level)
    store = VectorStore(settings.qdrant_url, settings.collection_name)
    await store.ensure_collection(settings.embedding_dim)
    yield
    await engine.dispose()
blocks.caption: lifespan function

blocks.text: Continuous Integration and Deployment Workflows

The repository utilizes GitHub Actions for CI and image building defined in .github/workflows/ci.yml [E4, E5, E6]. The test job installs dependencies, runs linters like ruff, and executes pytest [E6]. The image job builds the Docker image when pushes occur on the main branch [E6].

blocks.code:
name: ci
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: docqa
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - run: ruff check app tests
      - run: pytest -q

  image:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          push: false
          tags: docqa/api:latest
blocks.caption: CI workflow configuration

content.summary: This chapter examines database migrations and versions, focusing on the initial schema definition and its components.

blocks.text: Database Migrations and Versions
This chapter builds upon the Overview of FastAPI RAG Architecture. The details of data persistence and data models are covered in Data Models and Persistence.
Initial Schema Definition
The project uses Alembic for database migrations. The versions subsystem contains the migration scripts, such as the initial migration file [E3].
The upgrade function creates the initial tables for documents and chunks [E1].

blocks.code:
def upgrade() -> None:
    op.create_table(
        "documents",
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("filename", sa.String(512), nullable=False),
        sa.Column("content_type", sa.String(128), nullable=False),
        sa.Column("status", sa.String(32), nullable=False),
        sa.Column("raw_text", sa.Text, nullable=True),
        sa.Column("created_at", sa.DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=sa.func.now()),
    )
    op.create_table(
        "chunks",
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("document_id", sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey("documents.id", ondelete="CASCADE")),
        sa.Column("position", sa.Integer),
        sa.Column("text", sa.Text),
        sa.Column("token_count", sa.Integer),
    )
blocks.caption: Initial migration upgrade function defining documents and chunks tables
